why: Ezekiel 39:7 'So will I make my holy name known' follows 39:1 with Gog's defeat (39:2-6) skipped, so 'So' points at nothing

bridges.Ezekiel 39:7: God promises to break Gog's armies on the mountains of Israel, leaving them as food for birds and beasts, and to send fire on Magog.

why: Daniel 8:3 'before the river' and 8:16 'the banks of Ulai' refer to a place never named (8:2 dropped)

bridges.Daniel 8:3: In the vision Daniel finds himself at Shushan, beside the river Ulai.

why: The little horn that attacks the sanctuary (8:9-14) is skipped, yet Gabriel's interpretation of the fierce king at 8:23-25 depends on it; the man-like figure of 8:15 is also missing before 8:16

bridges.Daniel 8:16: From one of the four horns a small horn grows, attacks the sanctuary and stops the daily sacrifice. Then a figure like a man appears before Daniel.

why: Daniel 11:21 'in his estate' follows 11:4 with the long north-south wars (11:5-20) skipped, while the bridge describing those wars sits misplaced on 11:31, after the vile person has already appeared

bridges.Daniel 11:21: The messenger foretells generations of wars between the kings of the south and the kings of the north.
bridges.Daniel 11:31: This northern king invades the south, then, thwarted, turns in fury against God's holy covenant and his people.

why: Daniel 12:8 'I heard, but I understood not' follows 12:4 with nothing heard; the oath of the man in linen (12:5-7) is skipped

bridges.Daniel 12:8: Daniel then hears the man clothed in linen swear that the end of these wonders will come after 'a time, times, and an half.'

why: Hosea 4:17 introduces 'Ephraim', used throughout Hosea, with no explanation; a newcomer cannot tell it means Israel

bridges.Hosea 4:17: Hosea often calls the northern kingdom of Israel 'Ephraim,' after its leading tribe.

why: Zephaniah 1:12 'at that time' follows the book's heading directly (1:2-11 dropped), so the time referred to is never given

bridges.Zephaniah 1:12: The LORD announces that on the coming day of the LORD he will sweep away Judah's idolaters and punish Jerusalem's princes.

why: Zephaniah 2:11 'The LORD will be terrible unto them' has no antecedent; the oracles against Philistia, Moab and Ammon (2:4-10) are skipped

bridges.Zephaniah 2:11: Zephaniah pronounces doom on Judah's neighbors, the Philistines, and Moab and Ammon, who mocked God's people.

why: Zechariah 1:3 'Therefore say thou unto them' has nothing to follow from; restore the short 1:2 and drop the obscure 9:8 (9:4 flows straight into 9:9)
Zechariah 4:2 begins mid-sentence ('And said unto me') with no speaker; restore 4:1 and drop 5:4, which only elaborates 5:3's curse
